approach:
Root cause: after a squash the host's commit is not a descendant of the job's landed commit. `resync_tip` (land.rs:218) repairs that with `git.replay`, which rebuilds every later commit under new ids. The branch then leaves its remote copy's history, so a plain push is refused, and the drain never pushes. No parser or matching rule changes, so the refusal corpus is not involved.

Change: (1) `resync_tip` builds a merge commit with parents [head, merged]. The tree comes from `git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged)`, the commit from `git.commit_tree`, and the branch moves with the existing `reset_keep`. A conflict, or any difference in governed content from head, is an error and nothing moves. (2) `Athena::push_working_branch` makes a guarded plain push of the current branch. It skips the default branch, and it checks fast-forward with the existing `check_push` (pr.rs:300), with the current branch as the allowed branch. `after_merge` calls it after the resync, which covers `athena land --pr` and the drain's `PrLander`. (3) Each push has one owner. A defaulted `Lander::pushes_working_branch` is true for `PrLander`. `RealSteps::push_after_landing`, called by `Drain::land` after each `Landed` result, pushes only for a lander that does not push itself. (4) Landing intents and records skip commits named by an earlier landing record. (5) The gate stays unchanged. A gate test pins one known limit: the history walk before the cutover refuses a head that holds a landed job and its squash.

decisions.choice: Do not change the gate; resync_tip itself refuses any merge whose governed fingerprint differs from head's (`fingerprint(git,&tree,head) != fingerprint(git,head,head)`), naming the first path of `git.diff_tree(head,&tree)`. The branch is left unchanged.
decisions.reason: land_pr pushes the landed commit as the PR head (landing.rs:892-905) and main must be up to date before merging (System facts), so the squash tree equals the landed tree. merge_tree(landed,head,merged) then returns head's tree, and classify_pre_merge (invariant.rs:339-347) gives RecordsOnly by rule 4 with no edit. resync_tip never creates a merge whose governed content differs from the first parent's, so it cannot create a revert that passes as records only. A hand-made revert merge stays GovernedChange, and a test shows it.

rejected.option: Add a first rule to classify_pre_merge that accepts a merge taking paths verbatim from any parent
rejected.why: A second parent that is an ancestor of the first would let a merge revert governed content and still pass as RecordsOnly.

rejected.option: Tighten the gate to a one-sided merge
rejected.why: More gate code outside the request, for a case the host's up-to-date rule rules out. A refusal that leaves the branch unchanged is smaller.

rejected.option: Keep replay when main carries other governed content
rejected.why: The replay is the rewrite the request removes; that path would keep the divergence.

decisions.choice: Build the merge tree with merge_tree(base=landed, ours=head, theirs=merged), commit with commit_tree(parents [head, merged], sign=signs_commits), and move the branch with reset_keep.
decisions.reason: A plain `git merge` uses the real merge base. It conflicts whenever a later job edits lines the landed job added. With the landed commit as base, only the host's changes beyond the landed job come in. merge_tree (lib.rs:673), commit_tree (lib.rs:612) and reset_keep (lib.rs:759) exist, keep local edits and follow signing.

rejected.option: git merge in the work tree
rejected.why: Conflicts on later edits of landed lines, can leave a half-done merge, bypasses signing and keep-edits.

rejected.option: Keep replay and force-push or push_if_remote_at
rejected.why: Out of scope; treats the symptom.

decisions.choice: Exclude already-landed commits from landing intents and records using landing records, in gh/records.rs. For each landing record whose host_commit exists locally and is an ancestor of the expected base, pass its head_sha as `^head_sha` to a new `land::pr_commits_excluding`. `pr_commits` calls it with no exclusions.
decisions.reason: Under append-only, old landing commits stay in expected_base..head. throughput.rs:391-402 takes the newest landing record that holds a job's JobLanding commit as the job's landing time, so listing a landed job again moves its time and the new intent names old jobs. Messages are never read (land.rs:245-246), so a message marker is out. A landing whose record write failed (landing.rs:319-325) is listed again until reconciliation writes the record; this is stated in risks.

rejected.option: A marker line in the merge message
rejected.why: Free text deciding what is judged.

rejected.option: Exclude commits reachable from the first parent of any merge whose second parent is on the base
rejected.why: Anyone could hide a branch's history by making such a merge.

rejected.option: Also exclude heads of intents (critic finding 9)
rejected.why: Intents lack the host commit that proves the head reached main; reconcile writes the record from the intent, which closes the gap. Noted as a risk.

decisions.choice: One owner per push path (answers critic finding 8). `after_merge` owns the push for `athena land --pr` and for `PrLander`. A defaulted `Lander::pushes_working_branch(&self) -> bool {false}`, true for `PrLander`, lets `RealSteps::push_after_landing` skip the hook. The hook pushes only for a lander that does not push itself. `Drain::land` calls the defaulted `Steps::push_after_landing` after each Landed result.
decisions.reason: One push and at most one warning per landing. A drain test can drive RealSteps with a fake Lander that never reaches after_merge, and the PrLander path is shown by the after_merge test (athena land --pr needs the real gh and cannot be run in a test). Lander and Steps impls that do not override keep working: defaults.

rejected.why: The critic's finding 8: two owners.

rejected.option: Put the push only in commands::land and RealSteps::land
rejected.why: commands::land needs the real gh, so no test could show it.

rejected.option: A required Steps method
rejected.why: Every Steps double would change.

decisions.choice: The push helper is guarded (answers critic finding 4). It stays silent with no current branch or no origin. It skips with one line (`not pushing <branch> to origin: it is the default branch; changes reach it through pull requests`) when the current branch is `reconcile::local_default_branch(git,"origin")` (reconcile.rs:370), or, when origin/HEAD is not set, `main` or `master`. It then calls `check_push` with allowed_branch = the current branch, so a remote head that is not an ancestor of the local head is a warning. Last it pushes with GitRemote::push (plain). The CHANGELOG names the widened rule: Athena now also pushes the working branch.
decisions.reason: check_push (pr.rs:300) permits only the job's own branch and fast-forwards. The working branch is a second case, so the helper passes the current branch as the allowed branch and keeps the fast-forward test. The default branch is never pushed by Athena.

rejected.option: Push whatever is checked out
rejected.why: Would push local main straight to origin's main in fixtures and setups where the checkout is main.

rejected.option: Extend check_push with a working-branch field
rejected.why: Touches pr.rs and its callers (early.rs:277, landing.rs:560) for no gain.

decisions.choice: Before-the-cutover history walk (answers critic finding 5): no gate change. A gate test in athena-gate landing_tests.rs pins the shape. A branch holding job A's landed commit L and the host's squash S (as the merge's second parent) is refused by `check_history_with_exempt` with `job .. has already landed` (invariant.rs:738-746, history.rs:235-261). The CHANGELOG names the limit and a follow-up in the gate. The cutover-shown path (this repository's, athena.toml:153) judges only merge_base..tip with classify_pre_merge (history.rs:142-167) and is unaffected.
decisions.reason: The request requires the branch to descend from both its remote head and the merged main, so L and S are both reachable by construction. Making the walk tolerate it means a new gate rule (a squash that copies an earlier landing) and the user's agreement. Landing before the cutover is not unsupported: land_pr works without cutover_job (landing.rs:329). So the limit is stated, tested and put to the user.

rejected.option: Tolerate the shape in history.rs/invariant.rs now
rejected.why: Widens a governance rule outside the request without the user's agreement.

rejected.option: Declare pre-cutover landing unsupported
rejected.why: The code supports it.

decisions.choice:
Commit-shape table (critic finding 6). Columns: A=classify_pre_merge/classify_commit/pr_commits; B=check_pr_head (base=origin/main); C=check_history after the cutover (own commits merge_base..tip via classify_pre_merge, attribution on the part on main); D=check_history before the cutover (walk of every reachable commit); E=pr_commits_excluding in landing records; F=record_bases/close_carried_prs.
| Shape | A | B | C | D | E | F |
| job landing B on top of the merge | JobLanding | passes if verified | own commit, ok | first landing of B, ok | kept | its link is the landing; bases = open links whose head is an ancestor |
| earlier landed job commit L_A (stays on the branch) | JobLanding | ok (landing_problem is stateless) | own commit, ok | ok if first seen; refused with S (row S) | excluded by ^head_sha once A's landing record has a host commit on the base | an open earlier link at L_A stays an ancestor, so it is a base and is closed when carried (intended) |
| host squash S, second parent of the merge | not in base..head (on main) | not listed | on main: attribution via A's landing record | REFUSED 'already landed' with L_A: known limit, pinned by gate test | n/a | merged_commit, the closing target |
| resync merge M [head, S] | RecordsOnly (tree equals first parent's) | ok | own commit, RecordsOnly ok | multi-parent: parent_fps contains fp (invariant.rs:128-130), ok | kept; adds no job | n/a |
| records-only commit | RecordsOnly | ok | ok | unchanged | kept | n/a |
| owner-path commit | RecordsOnly where the rules exclude it | ok | ok | unchanged | kept | n/a |
| declared intervention before the last landing | DeclaredIntervention | ok only before a JobLanding in the range | ok | unchanged | kept | n/a |
| declared intervention after the last landing | DeclaredIntervention | offence (pr_check.rs:99-105), same as before | ok | unchanged | kept | n/a |
| retry-after-block landing | JobLanding (adds outcome-landed) | as a job landing | ok | chain rules unchanged | kept | as a job landing |
| hand edit of governed content | GovernedChange error | offence | violation (history.rs:153-166) | violation | n/a | n/a |
Tests: land.rs realistic-branch test (A, B, C, E, F rows), the hand-made revert merge test, gh/tests.rs landing_records_leave_out_landed_commits (E), land.rs record_bases test (F), gate landing_tests.rs pin test (D, row S).
decisions.reason: One row per shape, one column per reader, each cell tied to a test, so omitted readers show up.

steps: land.rs: rewrite `resync_tip`. Keep the two no-op checks. Call `git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged)`; `None` is an error saying the host's commit conflicts with the branch's later work and nothing moved. Then require `fingerprint(git,&tree,head)? == fingerprint(git,head,head)?`; otherwise error naming the first path of `git.diff_tree(head,&tree)`, nothing moved. Then `git.commit_tree(&tree, &[head, merged], message, sign)` with a plain subject such as `Merge the host's commit <short> into the branch` and no trailers. Remove the replay call and rewrite the doc comment (append-only; merge commit; no-op cases; errors).

land.rs: update `Athena::resync_onto_merge` docs and messages. Error context: `could not merge the host's commit {merged} into the branch; the branch is unchanged (it still holds {head})`. Success line: `the branch merged the host's commit {short}; it held {short} before`. Keep the lock, reset_keep and the unchanged-on-error text.

land.rs: add `pub fn pr_commits_excluding(git, remote_base, head, landed_heads: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<PrCommit>>`. It lists `rev-list --reverse base..head` plus `^<sha>` for each landed head that exists (`commit_exists`), then classifies as before with the same empty-range error. `pr_commits` calls it with an empty slice. Update the docs.

In order: `current_branch()` None -> silent false; `git.run(["remote","get-url","origin"])` error -> silent false; default branch (`reconcile::local_default_branch(&self.git,"origin")`, else `main`/`master`) -> print the one-line skip note, false; read `head()`; build `GitRemote{git:&self.git,name:"origin"}`; `remote_head(branch)`: if it equals head, true silently; else `check_push(&self.git, &PushRequest{allowed_branch:branch, branch, local_head:&head, remote_head})` and on refusal print `warning: could not push <branch> to origin: <refusal>; the landing stands`, false; else `remote.push(branch,&head)`; success prints `pushed <branch> to origin at <short>`, error prints the same warning. risks.risk: Append-only growth: squashed landing commits never become reachable from main, so every later head's own-commit range grows by each landing, and the CI history check and check_pr_head classify all of them each run.
risks.mitigation: Each old landing commit is a valid job landing and each resync merge classifies as records only, so the post-cutover checks pass; landing intents and records stay short through the record-based exclusion. A follow-up can apply the exclusion in history.rs and pr_check.rs. The CHANGELOG states the growth; per-job branches (D167) are the long-term answer.

risks.risk: The history walk before the cutover (no cutover_job, or a pending cutover) refuses a head that holds a landed job's commit and its squash.
risks.mitigation: Inherent to a branch that descends from both. Pinned by the gate test, stated in the CHANGELOG, and put to the user as an open question. The cutover-shown path used by this repository is unaffected and tested by the realistic-branch test.

risks.risk: resync_tip is stricter than the replay: governed content the host's commit carries and the branch lacks, or a file changed on both sides, is an error where the replay carried on.
risks.mitigation: The error names the first differing path and the branch is unchanged, as for a conflict; the maintainer merges by hand. The host requires main to be up to date, so the normal case gives a tree equal to head's. Tested as case (d) of criterion 4.

risks.risk: The push is refused, unreachable or skipped (default branch). The first landing after this change may be refused once if the remote copy was force-pushed by hand earlier.
risks.mitigation: A warning line gives the reason; the landing and the local resync stand. Once the maintainer reconciles the remote, the next landing pushes the whole append-only history with a plain push.

risks.risk: A landing whose record write failed (landing.rs:319-325) is listed again in the next intent until reconciliation writes the record (critic finding 9).
risks.mitigation: Reconciliation runs at the next `athena land` or `athena status` and writes the record from the intent, after which the exclusion applies. The listed commit is a valid job landing, so nothing is refused; only the next record is longer.

risks.risk: The Lander capability makes the RealSteps hook inactive for PrLander, so the drain's production push comes from after_merge and the hook runs only for other landers.
risks.mitigation: The after_merge test shows the PrLander path and a unit test pins that PrLander reports true; the tests/drain.rs tests show the hook and the skip. A lander that forgets to override pushes through the hook, which is safe because both use the same guarded helper.

risks.risk: Existing tests assume the rewritten shape (text needle, linear branch, main == C0).
risks.mitigation: The dependents list names each: the after_merge needle, the two land.rs resync tests and the two fixtures. The full suite and the per-crate runs in criterion 6 cover the rest.

risks.risk: The tests/drain.rs fake-agent fixture may not support two queued requests with one scenario script, and the Fixture checks out main.
risks.mitigation: Each new test switches to the branch `work` first. If two requests cannot be queued, the tests/drain.rs test lands one job and the Stub test shows the two-landing order; the producer reports this rather than weakening an assertion.

risks.risk: A slow ls-remote or push inside the drain's landing lock.
risks.mitigation: One ls-remote and at most one push per landing, with the same network exposure as the landing's own pushes; it holds no records or job state and a failure is only a warning.

demonstrations.method: A land.rs unit test on real git with a real bare repository. Build the landing scenario on the branch (job A landed, later job B, a hand edit). Run `git init --bare` in a tempdir, add it as `origin` and push the branch plainly, so the remote holds the previous head. Build the host squash as the existing resync test does (squash tree equal to the landed tree, parent = base). Call resync_tip and move the branch with reset_keep. Contrast in the same test: `git.replay(squash, landed, head, false)` gives a commit that is not a descendant of the previous remote head, and push_branch of it errors.
demonstrations.observes: is_ancestor(previous remote head, tip) and is_ancestor(squash, tip) are both true; git.push_branch("origin", branch, &tip) succeeds; the bare repository's branch equals tip; the replay contrast is refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the replay-based resync_tip the tip has one parent and is not a descendant of the previous remote head, so the is_ancestor(previous remote head, tip) assertion fails and the plain push is refused.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point athena_core::land::resync_tip (exists, land.rs:218) with its two no-op guards (merged already an ancestor of head; landed not on head). Fixture: the land.rs test helpers `repo()` (line 470) and `commit_message` (518), which exist, plus a bare repository made in the test with git init --bare and attached with `git remote add origin`; step 9 adds a small bare-repo helper. Nothing is faked; real git.

demonstrations.method: Three layers, one push per landing. (a) drain.rs unit test over the public `drain` entry point with the in-crate Stub: two Landed jobs give calls `[.., land job-a, push, .., land job-b, push]`; a rejected job gives no `push`. (b) tests/drain.rs drives `drain::drain` through RealSteps with a fake Lander on the existing Fixture. The test first runs `git checkout -b work` in the fixture (the Fixture checks out main, which the helper never pushes), adds a bare origin, pushes `work` once, queues two steward requests with distinct keys, and uses a lander that records at each ask the origin's `work` sha and the local head. It asserts: at the second ask the origin's `work` holds the head recorded at the first ask; after the drain the origin's `work` is an ancestor of the local head and holds the second landing's head; report.landed == 2. (c) A test with a lander that overrides `pushes_working_branch` to true: the origin's branch stays at its earlier sha, so the hook does not push twice; plus a unit test that `PrLander.pushes_working_branch()` is true. (d) A refused-push test: the origin first receives a sibling commit made with `git commit-tree` on the base commit and a plain push to the empty bare repo, so origin's `work` is not an ancestor of the local head. The drain shows report.landed == 1, landing text `landed`, the origin's `work` unchanged, and a captured Ui line starting `warning: could not push`. (e) Core tests of Athena::push_working_branch: a bare origin is pushed once and the second call is silent; an origin at a missing path warns and returns false; no origin and a detached HEAD are silent; a checkout on `main` is not pushed and prints the default-branch line; a checkout on a branch that origin/HEAD names as default is not pushed.

demonstrations.observes: (a) call order with one push per landing, none for a rejected job. (b) the origin's branch follows the local head after each landing. (c) no second push for a self-pushing lander. (d) a refused plain push is a warning and the job stays landed. (e) bare origin equals head after one push; the warning text for a missing origin; the default branch is never pushed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Drain::land call, Stub.calls has no `push` and the order assertion fails. Without the RealSteps override, the bare origin's branch stays at the earlier head and the ancestor assertions fail. Without the warning branch, test (d) finds no `warning: could not push` line. If the push were forced, the divergent origin in (d) would be overwritten and its tip would change. Without the default-branch skip, the main-checkout test finds main pushed.

demonstrations.method: land.rs unit tests on real repositories: (a) merged already an ancestor of head (a second run, and an older main commit as `merged`) returns None; (b) landed not on head returns None; (c) job B edits the line job A landed and the squash differs there: resync_tip errors with text containing `conflict` and head is unchanged; (d) the host's tree carries a governed file the branch lacks (main moved while the up-to-date rule was off): resync_tip errors naming the path and head is unchanged; (e) Athena::resync_onto_merge on case (c) returns an error saying the branch is unchanged and athena.head() is the same; (f) a hand-made merge of head with an older main commit that takes the older version of a governed file goes through land::classify_commit and is refused as GovernedChange.

User: The history check before the cutover (no cutover_job, or the cutover pending) will refuse a head that holds a landed job's commit and its squash, because a branch that descends from both is what the request requires. Is it acceptable to ship with that limit stated in the CHANGELOG and pinned by a gate test, with a gate follow-up, or must this job also change the history walk?

Should a follow-up update docs/enforcement.md (lines 64-68, which say Athena does not push), docs/design/native-pr-landing.md section 5.2a, and add a decision-log entry superseding D88's replay tradeoff? The plan leaves them out as outside the request's files.
